thread:
rachel-cs: Heads up — AcmeWidgets reported a spike of 502/timeout errors from their private VPC health probes after last night's cert refresh. They say it started ~02:00 UTC and affects internal /health endpoints only.

anya-support: ack, can you paste the probe failure logs and the hostname the probe hits? any recent firewall changes on their side? :mag:

rachel-cs: Log snippet from their probe agent: `tls: failed to verify certificate: certificate is not valid for requested name`
Host: internal-api.acme-prod.svc.redwood.local (they use split-horizon DNS). They did a cert rotation via our rotator at 01:48 UTC. No firewall changes reported on their ticket.

julian-sre: can we reproduce with openssl from our side into the VPC egress path? also need `dig` results for that internal name from their resolver and the cert SANs.

sam-eng: I ran a quick check via their support tunnel (limited):
```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -connect internal-api.acme-prod.svc.redwood.local:443 -servername internal-api.acme-prod.svc.redwood.local
depth=0 CN = api-2026.acme.internal
verify error:num=62:hostname mismatch
---
subject=/CN=api-2026.acme.internal
issuer=/CN=Acme-Internal-CA
---
```
The leaf cert CN is `api-2026.acme.internal` (no `.svc.redwood.local` SAN). Probe expects `internal-api.acme-prod.svc.redwood.local` and does strict name check.

anya-support: ohhh that's why. The new cert got generated with a short internal CN from their CA template (devops change?) — earlier certs had both names in SAN. Customer says they rotated using their internal CA; could be a template mismatch.

rachel-cs: They claim they used the same rotation job. Ticket includes rotator logs showing we uploaded their PEM bundle at 01:49:12. I attached the uploaded PEM in the ticket.

sam-eng: I inspected the uploaded bundle inside the rotation payload: the leaf cert's subjectAltName list is absent; it only has CN. Quick command I used: `openssl x509 -in leaf.pem -noout -text | sed -n '/Subject Alternative Name/,$p'` — shows nothing.

julian-sre: Two attack vectors: 1) name mismatch (probe fails), 2) if their health checker does OCSP/CRL validation we should ensure our egress allowlist doesn't block CRL/OCSP for their CA. Do we have any evidence of egress failures? devops-bot, do we have flow logs for their tenant egress around 01:50-02:05?

devops-bot: Flow logs: found 12 blocked outbound connections from tenant-acme-vpc/10.4.12.0/24 to crl.acme-internal.example (01:49:45–01:52:02). Firewall rule ID: fw-tenant-egress-2024-4. Blocking protocol: TCP/80.

anya-support: so both are true: the cert lacks SAN for the probe name AND our tenant firewall blocks outbound CRL fetch. That will make some clients fail hard.

rachel-cs: Customer has a canary job that uses strict hostname verification; they hit 502s on their LB because healthchecks are failing. They asked for an ETA — how fast can we get them a rollback or fix?

sam-eng: Short-term: we can patch our rotator to rewrite the cert bundle and add a SAN entry matching `internal-api.acme-prod.svc.redwood.local` before we push it, but that's risky. Safer: ask customer to reissue leaf cert with proper SANs (quick fix) or update their probe to accept CN (not ideal). For immediate mitigation we can add an exception to LB healthcheck to skip strict TLS name check for that target (requires config change on their LB or our proxy).

julian-sre: Operational plan: 1) tell customer to reissue cert with SANs (preferred). 2) temporarily allow egress to their CRL/OCSP endpoints in firewall (we can whitelist crl.acme-internal.example on fw-tenant-egress) — that should reduce validation failures. 3) if customer can't reissue immediately, we can back out last rotation (restore previous bundle) from rotator artifact at 01:30 UTC.

anya-support: I've DM'd the customer with the three options. They asked if we can automatically restore the previous bundle — yes/no?

sam-eng: Yes, we have a versioned artifact for their previous PEM. I can trigger a rollback if they authorize. Command I will run (dry-run first):
```
# show available uploads for tenant
$ redwood-rotator list-uploads --tenant acme --limit 5
# restore ID 42
$ redwood-rotator restore --tenant acme --upload-id 42 --apply
```
Will run once they confirm.

rachel-cs: Customer confirmed: do the rollback and temporarily whitelist crl.acme-internal.example. I'll update the ticket and ask them to reissue cert with SANs as follow-up.

julian-sre: I've opened a short-lived firewall exception (fw-tenant-egress allow crl.acme-internal.example tcp/80 for 2 hours) and documented rule id fw-temp-474. sam-eng — proceed with rollback when ready. :white_check_mark:

sam-eng: rollback applied at 02:12 UTC, LB healthchecks green at 02:18 UTC. Customer monitoring shows 0 errors since. I'll attach diffs and the commands to the ticket.

rachel-cs: Thanks team — customer confirmed service restored. Action items: (1) postmortem draft on cert template mismatch and a changelog to rotator validation to reject SAN-less uploads; (2) improve rotator safeguards to surface missing SANs for hostnames we know from tenant config; (3) ops playbook for quick egress whitelist. I'll create tickets. :memo:

anya-support: adding note: also alert customers during upload if the uploaded cert's CN doesn't match configured hostnames. Saves a lot of wakeups.

devops-bot: Incident closed by sam-eng (rollback & egress whitelist). Duration: 26 minutes.

rachel-cs: closing thread.
